title: Spanish Omelette
subtitle: Tortilla española with potato, onion, and egg
excerpt: A thick, set omelette of thinly sliced potato and onion cooked in olive oil, bound with beaten egg. Served warm or at room temperature, cut into wedges. One of the great dishes of Spain.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tortilla española (Spanish omelette) is one of the defining dishes of Spanish cuisine, eaten at breakfast, lunch, dinner, and as tapas at any hour. It is a fundamentally simple dish: potatoes and onions cooked slowly in olive oil until very tender, then combined with beaten eggs and cooked in the same pan. The controversy in Spain over whether a proper tortilla includes onion (many Spanish cooks insist it should not) is one of the great culinary debates of the country. The correct texture of the interior is a matter of personal preference: some prefer it fully set throughout, others prefer the centre to remain slightly creamy. The tortilla is flipped halfway through cooking, which requires confidence: a wide plate or a pan lid is placed over the pan and the whole thing inverted in a single motion. This is the technique that most people find intimidating but it is simply a matter of speed and commitment.

recipeTools.notes: A 24 cm non-stick frying pan with a lid or wide plate for flipping.

content.text: The potatoes and onion must be fully tender before the eggs go in. Cook them slowly in a generous amount of olive oil over medium-low heat: the oil confits the potato, leaving it soft and sweet. Do not rush: the potato must be completely tender and yielding, not al dente. To flip the tortilla, place a large flat plate over the pan, invert the whole thing in one quick motion, and slide the tortilla back in. Have the plate close before you start.

Heat the olive oil in a 24 cm non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the potato and onion slices, season with salt, and turn to coat in the oil. Cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning occasionally, until the potato is completely tender and the onion is soft and sweet. Drain off most of the oil (reserve it).
Beat the eggs in a bowl and season with salt and pepper. Add the cooked potato and onion mixture to the eggs and stir gently to combine. Leave to rest for 5 minutes.

Return 2 tablespoons of the reserved oil to the pan over medium heat. Pour in the egg and potato mixture. Shake the pan to settle the mixture. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the base is set and the edges are firm. Place a large flat plate over the pan and quickly invert the tortilla onto the plate. Slide it back into the pan and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more until just set. Rest for 5 minutes before cutting into wedges.
